findings.passage: “Today’s vote was a critical step towards restoring Americans’ confidence in our elections.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name on House passage of H.R. 8281, the SAVE Act, which the release says would require proof of citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. He calls the vote a step toward restoring confidence in elections.

findings.passage: The fact remains—the SAVE Act is our only tool to ensure American votes decide American elections. It’s the law of the land in Florida and contributes to the security and integrity of our model election system.  I was pleased this bill passed with bipartisan support, and I remain committed to fighting for election integrity in Congress.”
findings.note: Same release. He describes the SAVE Act as the only tool to make sure American votes decide American elections, says it is law in Florida, and says he will keep working on election integrity in Congress. Elsewhere in the release he links the bill to non-citizen voting.

findings.passage: While the vast majority of Americans oppose noncitizen voting, many states continue to find noncitizens on their voter rolls due to inadequate safeguards. The SAVE Act helps address this by requiring states to verify citizenship when registering individuals to vote in federal elections.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name after he voted for H.R. 22, the SAVE Act (220-208). He ties the bill to non-citizens found on state voter rolls and to states checking citizenship at registration.

findings.passage: I urge the Senate to pass this bill and send it to the president’s desk.”
findings.note: Same release. He asks the Senate to pass H.R. 22 and send it to the president.
